title: Why Learn on the Device
summary: Work through Why Learn on the Device.

blocks.md: This lesson follows **Why Learn on the Device** in *Edge Intelligence* (Vol II).

blocks.source: Vol II, Edge Intelligence, § Why Learn on the Device
blocks.md: A distribution gap justifies spending device resources only when centralized retraining cannot close it in time or within policy. A cloud-trained model that relies on a server round trip or a raw-data upload for every adjustment fails whenever a user has an unfamiliar accent, a remote sensor loses connectivity, a regulation forbids exporting personal traces, or millions of devices would overwhelm backend ingestion. Those four pressures (personalization, latency and availability, privacy, and infrastructure efficiency) motivate shifting learning to the edge.

blocks.title: Map of the section

The section is organised as:

- Simpler alternatives first

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Local training must earn its place matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Centralized, local-only, and federated learning differ in what crosses the device boundary, and local training is justified only when a measured adaptation gain beats feature-based personalization under privacy and resource constraints.

questions.q: The section **Why Learn on the Device** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: On-device data is sparse, weakly labeled, non-IID, and unshuffleable, so few-shot sets, streaming updates, replay buffers, and compressed representations each spend a different scarce resource, and an embedding is not anonymized by being low-dimensional.

A returned update is meaningful only against its base version and schema, so the coordinator binds updates to version and round, reconciles devices returning after days offline, and down-weights stale contributions in buffered asynchronous aggregation.

Freezing removes a parameter's gradient and optimizer state but not its place on the backward path, so bias-only updates, LoRA, and residual adapters each shrink a different term of the peak-memory budget.

Centralized, local-only, and federated learning differ in what crosses the device boundary, and local training is justified only when a measured adaptation gain beats feature-based personalization under privacy and resource constraints.
